parameters.content:
## The search itself

This is the workhorse: it reads your funding profile, searches the
official sources for your country and state plus non-government money,
checks each new program against its own official page, and saves a short
report.

**Nothing here decides when it runs.** Your agent starts it when you ask,
and a scheduler can start it on a clock later. Both call this same
workflow, so there is only ever one copy of the actual searching.

It takes a few minutes. The report is saved for your agent to read back
in the chat; nothing is sent anywhere else. It never applies for anything
and never contacts anyone.

## What one search costs

Up to ten searches per beat, four page checks, one eligibility pass.
The ceiling was three until a run showed the model being refused thirteen
times and dropping real programs for want of another look. Budget one to
two dollars; most runs use well under the ceiling.

Every run records its own searches and tokens in `funding_runs`, so after
a few goes you can read the real number instead of trusting an estimate.

To spend less, remove a beat from your profile.

const collected = $('Collect Verified').first().json;
const context = $('Check Profile').first().json;

const programs = collected.verified.map((program, index) => ({
  index,
  programName: program.programName,
  administeredBy: program.administeredBy,
  amountText: program.amountText,
  whatItFunds: program.whatItFunds,
  closesAt: program.closesAt,
  status: program.status,
  effort: program.effort,
  eligibility: program.eligibility,
}));

const user = [
  'The business:',
  context.profileJson,
  '',
  'The programs, with the eligibility criteria taken from their official pages:',
  JSON.stringify(programs, null, 1),
  '',
  'For each program return one entry:',
  '{"verdicts":[{"index":0,"verdict":"eligible|likely|unclear|not-eligible","verdictReason":"","deciderCriterion":"","priority":0}]}',
  '',
  'verdictReason is the single criterion that decides it, in one plain sentence.',
  'deciderCriterion is what the owner has to check for themselves.',
  'priority is 0 to 100: sooner deadlines and better fit score higher, and more application effort scores lower.',
].join('\n');

return [{ json: { requestBody: {
  model: 'claude-opus-5',
  max_tokens: 16000,
  thinking: { type: 'adaptive' },
  output_config: { effort: 'high' },
  system: "You read published eligibility criteria against one business's profile and say what the criteria imply.\n\nRules:\n- You cannot confirm eligibility. Only the administering body can. Your verdict is a reading of published criteria, nothing more.\n- Never write that the business is eligible. Write what the criteria say and what the owner has to check.\n- Where a criterion depends on something the profile does not contain, the verdict is 'unclear' and you name what is missing.\n- Return JSON and nothing else: no explanation, no markdown fence.",
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: user }],
} } }];

const report = $('Write Report').first().json;
const reported = new Set(report.reportedFingerprints ?? []);
const stamp = report.ranAt;

return (report.findings ?? []).map((finding) => ({ json: {
  fingerprint: finding.fingerprint,
  firstSeenAt: stamp,
  lastSeenAt: stamp,
  reportedAt: reported.has(finding.fingerprint) ? stamp : '',
  programName: finding.programName,
  administeredBy: finding.administeredBy,
  officialUrl: finding.officialUrl,
  sourceTrust: finding.sourceTrust,
  kind: finding.kind,
  amountText: finding.amountText,
  whatItFunds: finding.whatItFunds,
  opensAt: finding.opensAt,
  closesAt: finding.closesAt,
  status: finding.status,
  eligibilitySummary: finding.eligibilitySummary,
  verdict: finding.verdict,
  verdictReason: finding.verdictReason,
  deciderCriterion: finding.deciderCriterion,
  effort: finding.effort,
  contentHash: finding.contentHash,
  dismissed: 'no',
} }));
